title: Tap as improvisation and dancing to Paul Robeson's River Stay Away
summary: Green says Bubbles introduced a new technique like improvisation in jazz, recites River Stay Away From the Door, and says he danced to Robeson.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well, how was tap dancing starting to change in terms of just the technique and the style at this particular time?
No -- how was it beginning to change?
This rhythm, this -- say, this was a new method. It was a new technique, a new technology, you know. Like a new -- I think they call it improvisation in music, like when you go to --

Yes. When you go to a release, see -- releasing in music is like an augment -- an augment, and you go into the middle of the song, which they say was channel, see. And you go and finish like -- I'm trying to think of some song.
"You Keep Going Your Way", I think -- that's what it was. "River Stay Away From the Door" -- that's what it was, 'River Stay Away from the Door.' That explained a lot about jazz --
It went, "You ain't going -- you keep going your way, you ain't going my way. River stay away from the door." Like that -- "Don't come up any higher, 'cause I'm all alone.
Just leave me my bed and fire, and that is all I own." You see. "I'll keep going my way and you keep going your way. River stay away from the door." Yeah. Paul Robertson, he sang that.
Did you tap dance to Paul Robeson?
